title: KV cache namespace bleed and eviction-threshold oscillation remediation
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Summary: During a mid-sized capacity surge (03/09-03/10) several tenants experienced elevated memory growth and degraded request latency. Investigation showed cross-namespace entries persisted in KV cache shards and eviction behavior oscillated under bursty load patterns, causing backpressure and eventual OOMs on a subset of serving nodes. This ticket tracks remediation work, short-term mitigations and long-term design changes to eliminate namespace bleed and stabilize eviction thresholds.
timeline: 2026-03-09 02:18 UTC - On-call alerted: increased pod memory usage and rising tail latency on /generate route
2026-03-09 02:45 UTC - Rolling restart of affected nodes to restore capacity (temporary relief), incident declared Sev2
2026-03-09 03:30 UTC - Initial hotfix deployed: fallback eviction policy enforced (aggressive immediate-evict), reduced memory growth but increased latency for cold requests

2026-03-10 11:00 UTC - Root cause triage: discovered namespace key mis-assignment when shard rebalancer applied async migration during autoscale; combined with hysteresis bug in eviction score decay led to eviction-threshold oscillation
2026-03-11 09:00 UTC - Hotfix 2 deployed: per-shard namespace validation and conservative eviction hysteresis added; started scrub job to remove contaminated entries
2026-03-12 14:00 UTC - Memory growth stabilized, tail latencies returned to baseline for most tenants.
root_cause_summary: A race between shard rebalancer (async in-place migration) and concurrent write/eviction logic caused a subset of entries to be stamped with the wrong tenant namespace token. The eviction score decay function included an adaptive threshold that, under bursty write/delete patterns, oscillated between elevated and depressed thresholds; combined, these two issues allowed contaminated entries to survive longer than expected and prevented the eviction system from making forward progress on eviction under load.
steps_taken: Rolled back the async in-place migration path for the rebalancer to a safer stop-and-copy mode (short-term mitigation) — rolled out to affected clusters by 2026-03-09 12:00 UTC
Deployed per-shard namespace validation checks at write and compaction time to reject cross-namespace insertions (hotfix 2026-03-10-namespace-guard)
Introduced eviction hysteresis clamp to prevent rapid threshold toggling under bursty patterns (hotfix 2026-03-11-evict-hysteresis)
Started a rolling scrub/sweep job to identify and delete contaminated keys with mismatched namespace tokens (scrub run id: SCRUB-20260310-01)
Increased telemetry and alerting for per-tenant memory share and per-shard sustained-unproductivity windows
action_items: AI-1: Replace async in-place rebalancer with versioned copy-rebalance and atomic swap in runtime — owner: Evan Chu — due: 2026-03-20
AI-2: Add permanent per-entry namespace integrity field to on-disk index and enforce at read/write — owner: Maria Lopez — due: 2026-04-02
AI-3: Rewrite eviction score decay algorithm to include minimum hold window and backoff cap (add unit tests covering oscillation scenarios) — owner: Priya Nair — due: 2026-03-28
AI-4: Implement tenant-memory-quotas with hard cap + soft-reactive eviction and circuit-breaker to prevent single tenant OOMs — owner: Jonas Meyer — due: 2026-04-10
AI-5: Create a scheduled scrub tool and runbook (how to detect, run, and verify scrub) and surface to Console as maintenance job — owner: SRE Team (lead: Kunal Patel) — due: 2026-03-24
AI-6: Add chaos/rebalance scenario to CI (simulate rebalancer concurrent writes, eviction churn) — owner: Reliability QA — due: 2026-04-15
AI-7: Postmortem review with Product & Design to discuss tenant communication and status page templates for cache contamination incidents — owner: Aisha Khatri — due: 2026-03-18
telemetry_changes: New metric: kvcache.per_shard.namespace_mismatch_rate (counts mismatched namespace write attempts)
New alert: sustained per_shard.unproductive_eviction_time > 5m triggers pager
Dashboard: eviction-threshold-time-series with overlay of write/delete rate and rebalance events
rollout_plan: Staged rollout: 1) Deploy namespace-integrity checks and hysteresis clamp to canary pool (5% nodes) for 48h with synthetic load; 2) Expand to 30% with increased scrubbing frequency; 3) Full cluster rollout after 7 days without regressions. Each step gated by health checks (memory growth, p95 latency, eviction throughput).
notes: PM feedback (2026-03-11): communicate a concise timeline and customer impact summary to support; ensure templated status messages are ready
Design review scheduled 2026-03-15 to discuss Console UX for scheduled scrub jobs and maintenance windows
SRE: consider pre-provisioning extra buffer nodes during rolling rebalance to avoid pressure spikes
